content.thinking:
I'm laying out the postmortem: the symptom is account page requests failing for many shoppers, with G5309 and Gbac1 as the evidence. The first causal step is those failed requests, and the second is a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 that began at 19:28.

Next I'm checking which earlier changes the record rules out: the flag was off until 19:27, and account pages rendered normally before then, so the flag switch is the likely trigger.

I'm checking whether a deploy could explain it, and the one-day deploy query came back empty, so the flag switch stands out. The metrics show the service at baseline until 19:28 under the same revision, so that revision is an unlikely cause.

I'm checking whether the earlier changes are ruled out: the flag switch is the only recorded change, and the service was at its baseline before 19:28 with the same revision still running, while reverting the flag brought it back to normal. Next I'm looking at the failing code path itself, where the spend-per-item average divides by a count of this month's purchases that comes out empty for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month, and the account page turns that error into a failed page. The line 47 error fits division by zero, but the empty-list mechanism itself rests only on that reading, not on a confirmed run.

I'm drafting the contributing-factors section now: the monthly spend path wasn't tested for shoppers with no purchases this month, so the fault would have surfaced in tests if they had covered it.

I'm drafting the second contributing factor now: the flag went to all traffic at once, with no staged rollout seen, so a smaller first share would have limited the impact and surfaced the error sooner. I'm proposing a progressive rollout gated on error rate for flags like this one.

I'm deciding which action items to keep: the alert fired within the accounted window, so detection isn't a real contributing factor. Staged rollout and the tests-with-flag-on requirement are the two solid fixes, and I'm wiring each to its contributing factor. I'm still weighing whether a detection item adds anything.

I'm keeping the flag off for now, since the fault is still in the code and turning the flag back on could fail account pages again for shoppers with no purchases this month.

I'm writing out the root-cause statement now: the monthly spend average divides by the count of this month's purchases, and that is the step that breaks for shoppers with none.

I'm working out the write-up's last open pieces: the root-cause sentence should say the empty list makes the division fail with ZeroDivisionError, which the account page turns into a failed page, without leaning on any figure. I'm also noting that the investigator's onset call at 19:28, tied to the flag change, held up, and I'm checking how its candidate was timed in the record.

I'm noting what went well in the response: the investigator placed the onset at 19:28 and named the flag change as the candidate cause, which later held up. The mitigation side switched the flag off and confirmed recovery in the metrics before calling it mitigated, and the code-fix side has a draft PR in review.

I'm checking whether anything else could have caused the failures before settling on the flag change. No deploy showed up in the day before the onset, and the same revision kept running after the flag was turned off and the pages came back, so the revision is unlikely to be the cause.

I'm pinning down the first two causal steps: the account page requests failed, and then they raised ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, which didn't appear in the logs before the onset minute. The ClientDisconnected errors that show up before the flag change were already there at baseline, so I'm setting them aside as unrelated to the incident.

I'm writing out the timeline steps: the flag was switched on by an admin in one minute, and from then on every evaluation was on, so the account page took the new spend-summary path. The last step is that with the flag on, the spend summary likely computes a this-month average per item, which can't be computed for shoppers with no purchases this month.

I'm wrapping up the root-cause write-up now, and I'm settling on the ending that frames the account page failure as the result of the flag change.

action_items.item: Require the tests for any flag-gated code path to run with the flag on as well as off, and block switching the flag on in production until they pass.
Switch flags such as monthly-spend-feature on in stages, starting with a small share of shoppers, and hold each stage while the account page error rate is watched.
Keep monthly-spend-feature off until the fix proposed in PR #578, or another fix, has been reviewed and merged.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. This error first appears in the onset minute, and the logs read from before it show no such error.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: none came back for the day read before the onset. The revision running on every replica stayed in place after the flag was turned off, and the service went back to normal.
The ClientDisconnected failures on account pages (shoppers closing the connection): these were already in the logs before the flag change, while account pages rendered normally.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests started taking the new spend-summary path when admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The flag's evaluations split between off and on during that minute and were all on in every minute after it.
With the flag on, the spend summary likely computes a this-month average per item that cannot be computed for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly spending summary made account pages fail for shoppers, likely because the summary divides by the number of items bought this month and some shoppers had bought nothing this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag could be switched on in production, no check was seen that ran the monthly spend path with the flag on for a shopper with no purchases this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division error would have been found before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from off to on for all shoppers at once. No staged rollout or error-rate guard tied to the flag change was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit failing account pages, and the rollout could have been stopped before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent named the flag change as the candidate cause, C1, after reading metrics, change events and logs. The confirmed action later bore it out.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature from on to off. This change can be put back.
The Mitigation Agent checked the service's metrics before it judged the action confirmed, instead of assuming the revert had worked.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #578 for a person to review.
The log lines showed the flag's evaluations splitting between off and on in the minute the errors began, which tied the errors to the flag change directly.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, which divides the month's spend by the number of purchases marked `in_current_month`. For a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that list is empty, so the division at line 47 raises ZeroDivisionError, and the boundary in src/io_shop/account_page.py turns each error into a failed account page.
input.still_at_risk: Turning monthly-spend-feature back on could make account pages fail again as they did here.
